answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to one costly vertex in a verified work graph: joining requires completing a unique, peer-checked task and staking a refundable deposit. Like a pearl forming around a single grain, reputation grows slowly at that vertex over a long horizon of work, not on fresh copies. Spawning thousands of fakes means paying thousands of deposits, doing thousands of checked tasks, and waiting through the slow horizon, while honest agents keep their history. Fakes cost work and capital but earn nothing until proven, so flooding stops paying.
